basis: Complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy defines renal injury, hemolysis and thrombocytopenia; hypertension occurs in 30–79%.
Orbital disorder causing pulsatile protrusion of the eye; an underlying vascular cause is not established for every case.
Progressive macular degeneration impairs central vision; extraocular findings are explicitly rare.
Loss of smell belongs to the neurologic axis; nasal inflammation and infections are possible causes, not universal features.
Malignant odontogenic epithelial tumour arising in the tooth-forming apparatus, typically as a destructive intraosseous jaw tumour.
Isolated small-eye malformation with severe hypermetropia; associated pressure and retinal abnormalities remain within the ocular axis.
Mitochondrial energy-metabolism defect with lactic acidosis; neonatal encephalopathy is characteristic and common (>30%); hypotonia alone does not establish muscle damage.
PTH resistance causes calcium-phosphate dysregulation despite normal renal function; skeletal abnormalities vary substantially across subtypes.
Spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia defines abnormal vertebral and epiphyseal skeletal development; no additional organ involvement is established.
Valve/aortic, skeletal and skin abnormalities define MASS; myopia is a common defining feature (>30%). Dural ectasia alone does not establish neural damage.
Hereditary progressive sensorineural hearing loss; neural deafness remains within the hearing axis.
Glandular tumour of vulvar reproductive structures, including vestibular and Bartholin glands; no represented organ axis.
Congenital endocrine pancreatic insulin excess causes hypoglycemia; persistent neurologic damage is not established in at least 30% of this specific subtype.
Inherited retinal degeneration; no syndromic extraocular involvement is specified.
Congenital multivalvular dysplasia with common regurgitation; extra-cardiac structural findings are occasional or very rare.
Cyst confined to the prostate, a reproductive organ; urinary tract damage is not inherent to the concept.
Locally invasive carcinoma originating in the esophageal epithelium; metastasis is uncommon.
Isolated hereditary displacement of the ocular lens without systemic involvement.
Immune-mediated chronic polyarthritis; ANA positivity increases uveitis risk, but ocular disease is not reliably present in at least 30% of this subgroup.
Eyelid eversion is an ocular adnexal disorder; spasm does not establish a separate neurologic disease.
The supplied definition and frequent encephalitis annotations establish invasive CNS amoebic infection; visual loss is occasional and photophobia alone is insufficient.
Inheritance-pattern umbrella rather than an organ-defined disease; no organ axis applies consistently across its heterogeneous descendants.
Hereditary early-onset parkinsonism and intellectual disability define CNS dysfunction; rigidity is neurologic rather than primary muscle disease.
Hypomyelinating CNS degeneration; joint contractures occur in 4/5 and scoliosis in 2/3. Nystagmus and gaze abnormalities reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Ependymal tumour originating in the spinal cord.
